_decision: darkActiveBg = oklch(0.39 0 0). The background of the rail button for the section currently selected. Value from proposedDarkRailTokens, the approved decision record — not from measuring the component.
_state: `selected`, not `rest`. It was declared `rest` while the vocabulary had no word for persistent current, which was truthful only because the demo happens to select Slides — if the default section ever changed, this check would fail for a reason unrelated to the token. `selected` is a verified no-op: the runner requires the element to already carry a real marker and records which one, so pointing this at an unselected button now fails instead of silently measuring the wrong state.
_serialisation: The expected string is the COMPUTED spelling. tokens.css authors some colours as oklch(55.6% 0 0) while the browser computes oklch(0.556 0 0) — the same colour, and compare() is exact string equality. proposedDarkRailTokens already uses the computed spelling. Never resolve a mismatch by pasting the measured value.
_scope: KNOWN LIMIT, stated so a pass is not read as more than it is: FullRailPreview renders this colour from proposedDarkRailTokens via colorsFor(), which is the same array this expectation is copied from. The check therefore proves the value survives the render — plumbing, cascade and timing — and CANNOT prove the value is correct. --sidebar-rail-* exists in no file under tokens/; these are proposals, not shipped tokens. Independent verification arrives when they are authored as real tokens and this expectation can point at those instead.
